transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Saturday, November 21. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Man poses as Lawrence Bishnoi's kin to extort Delhi businessman. A businessman has come forward with disturbing claims of extortion threats, where he was asked for rupees 60 lakh, accompanied by a half-cut rupees 10 note as a chilling message. Police investigations led them to Ashu Maurya after analyzing delivered envelopes and reviewing CCTV footage. Maurya ultimately confessed to the crime, driven by financial struggles, and revealed prior acquaintance with the victim's family. Dario Amodei to Jamie Dimon: Why Anthropic avoids hiring highly technical people. Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, emphasized the importance of cultural alignment in hiring. The company values a cohesive workplace more than merely individual expertise. To maintain this, Anthropic carefully evaluates applicants to ensure they share the company's cultural ideals. Their rigorous interview process has kept all seven co-founders engaged since the company was founded. Adani project work on at village not listed in clearance: Official. Adani Green Energy Ltd's Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar. Concerns have been raised regarding approvals from the National Board for Wildlife and environmental clearances. The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board is looking into these allegations and has conducted inspections. An honorary wildlife warden has requested a detailed inquiry into the project's compliance with regulations. Oregon mother sues couple for $8.7m after son loses eye on e-bike at sleepover. A negligence lawsuit has emerged following a tragic e-bike accident involving a 14-year-old boy during a birthday sleepover hosted by Tessa and Matthew Cohen. The allegations claim that the Cohens provided electric bikes without adequate supervision or safety protocols. As a result, the boy sustained life-altering injuries, requiring significant medical attention. The lawsuit demands $8.7 million in damages to address his painful recovery and its long-term consequences. 12 versus 9: KL Rahul way ahead of Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma. KL Rahul achieved a significant milestone by scoring his 13th Test century against New Zealand in Wellington. This century places him among India's most successful Test openers in history. He has now scored a total of twelve centuries as an opener, surpassing Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma. Additionally, he has completed the rare feat of scoring centuries in all four SENA countries. 'My village was occupied by China': Rijiju hits Rahul with 4 questions over PM jibe. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday hit back at Rahul Gandhi over his "compromised PM" jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 'Look at India': Trump takes India's 7 percent growth as cue to demand Fed rate cuts. US President Donald Trump on Friday criticised the Federal Reserve over its interest rate policy, citing India's economic growth as an example of how lower borrowing costs could support expansion. Ahmedabad student turns fatal fall into safety mission for 1 lakh workers. Project Wave, spearheaded by Shiv Mandlik, emerged from his recognition of the dangers faced by construction workers and their families. This initiative is dedicated to raising safety awareness and supplying modern protective gear, having already reached more than 105,000 workers through training, equipment provision, and welfare support in various cities. Beyond safety, it tackles vital concerns like housing and hygiene, demonstrating Mandlik's unwavering commitment to the well-being of construction laborers. Louisiana farmer wins $59,967 after neighbours clear trees from 18ft land strip. In a landmark ruling, Louisiana farmer Benjamin Lee Bird emerged victorious in a lengthy 13-year battle over a disputed land strip. The court upheld his ownership, leading to a damages award against his neighbours for their actions, which included tree removal and altering drainage systems on Bird's land. The appeals court confirmed his rights, adjusting the compensation to $59,966. Fake university list grows from 20 to 32 in 3 years, 18 old names still on it. University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued a fresh public advisory warning students and parents against enrolling in unrecognised institutions, even as its list of fake universities has grown from 20 to 32 in three years. SBI told to pay Aligarh man rupees 5,000 daily for failing to return house deed. An elderly man in Aligarh struggled to retrieve his original property deed from the State Bank of India. After repaying his home loan in 2019, he requested the deed's return multiple times. Following the bank's failure to comply, he filed a complaint in June 2023. The consumer commission ruled in his favor and mandated SBI to pay compensation.

The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) on Friday said it alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) about reports of the alleged use of Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys to increase gold's weight, and urged the industry and consumers to remain vigilant. "While there have been media reports from certain quarters regarding the possible misuse of materials such as Rhenium and Iridium in gold, we want to assure the entire jewellery industry and all gold buyers that there is absolutely no reason to panic. The Bureau of Indian Standards is treating the matter with utmost seriousness," GJC Chairman Rajesh Rokde said in a statement.
